subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Does any supported ACP client path outside the named files allow an untrusted client to submit recursive or otherwise attacker-shaped historical-log filters, or is the ledger intentionally limited to the fixed bounded lookups visible on current main?
rationale: Source inspection disproves the report's stated data flow, but repository policy reserves protected security-boundary disposition for a human owner who can confirm the complete externally reachable protocol surface.

options.title: Confirm boundary and close
options.body: Confirm that ACP ledger queries are restricted to the current fixed lookups and close the report as not reproducible on current main.

options.title: Request concrete exploit payload
options.body: Ask the reporter for the exact ACP request, route, authentication state, and measurable database or CPU impact before considering code changes.

options.title: Sponsor defense-in-depth limits
options.body: If broader history filtering is supported or planned, define route-level complexity, concurrency, and query-budget policy with abuse-focused tests.

recommendation.title: Confirm boundary and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that ACP ledger queries are restricted to the current fixed lookups and close the report as not reproducible on current main.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to both the original ACP surface and later session-security hardening.
